title: Incident Evidence Pipeline Retrospective and Next Steps
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures the postmortem-style retrospective from the Nov incident where evidence ingestion lag and partial SIEM export caused delayed triage. Goal: capture concrete gaps in the evidence pipeline, propose low-risk mitigations and prioritized work, and align owners for RBAC v2 / audit-schema changes that will improve automated evidence collection for future incidents.

Executive summary (tl;dr):
- Root cause: evidence ingestion pipeline throttled by sudden audit-event spike from RBAC migration cadence; normalization workers fell behind and the SIEM exporter dropped non-critical events to avoid overload.
- Impact: delayed availability of canonical forensic evidence for 2.5 hours; one escalation required manual harvest by on-call.
- Key gaps: (1) audit schema missing correlation_id on some RBAC-change events, (2) lack of backpressure signaling from SIEM exporter into normalization queue, (3) no canary for evidence completeness during releases that touch RBAC, (4) weak chain-of-custody metadata persisted for automated snapshots.

Observed timeline (high level):
- 2024-11-19 09:12 UTC: RBAC v2 rollout job triggered (gradual, but bursty due to retry behavior).
- 09:18 UTC: auditProducer spiked to 6x baseline; messages queued in evidence-ingest topic.
- 09:20 UTC: normalization worker pool autoscaled but delayed due to cold-starts in eu-west nodes.
- 09:25 UTC: SIEM exporter started dropping low-priority events when export buffer > 80% (fallback configured).
- 09:26–11:50 UTC: partial evidence persisted; correlation_id absent on ~14% of RBAC-change events leading to orphaned artifacts.
- 11:50 UTC: on-call manually harvested raw logs from primary audit bucket and reconstructed chain-of-custody for the critical window.

Concrete technical gaps and notes: 
1) Missing correlation_id at source:
- Several RBAC change producers (legacy admin API handler) did not populate correlation_id. Without it, the normalizer cannot link action -> actor -> resource across multiple microservice events.
- Recommendation: mandate correlation_id in audit log schema v2; add enforcement to producer client lib and linting step in CI.

2) Audit schema fields to add/standardize:
- correlation_id (string)
- actor_type (enum: user, service, integration)
- actor_id (string)
- action (string) e.g., rbac.grant, rbac.revoke, token.create
- target_resource.type (string) -> flattened as resource_type (for compatibility)
- target_resource.id (string) -> resource_id
- ip_address (string)
- user_agent (string)
- trace_id (string)
- auth_method (enum: password, oauth, service_key)
- rbac_delta (string) -> short textual diff of permission change
- evidence_hash (hex) -> optional precomputed hash for binary blobs

3) Normalization and backlog behavior: 
- Normalizer should persist raw offsets until normalized message acked by both internal store and SIEM exporter; current design marks offset consumed on enqueue only.
- Add durable-staging area (cold bucket) and ack semantics: consume -> write raw -> normalize -> write normalized -> export -> mark offset committed.

4) SIEM exporter resiliency: 
- Current circuit-breaker drops events when export buffer full; no automatic retry window per message class.
- Proposal: implement a small priority retry queue with exponential backoff for forensic events (rbac.*, auth.*) and a fast-path for critical tags (correlation_id present).

5) Chain-of-custody and evidence automation: 
- When automation snapshots resources, include: snapshot_id, evidence_hash, signed_by (KMS key id), kms_signature, storage_path, retention_policy, collection_timestamp.
- Evidence ingestion pipeline should stamp signed tokens so manual harvests can be validated later.

6) Observability gaps: 
- No metric for evidenceCompletenessRatio which would have signaled missing correlation links.
- Require dashboards: evidence-ingest-lag, normalization-queue-depth, siem-export-drop-rate, evidence-completeness-ratio by service.

Playbook/operational changes (short-term <= 2 weeks):
- Mandatory change: Update producer lib to require correlation_id; rollout to RBAC producers first. Owner: Liam Chen. Due: 2024-12-10.
- Add alert: normalization-queue-depth > 5000 for > 5m -> notify sec-oncall + infra-scaling. Owner: Zoe Carter. Due: 2024-12-01.
- Deploy small hotfix: enable durable-staging persistence for evidence-ingest topic to prevent offset loss if normalizers fall behind. Owner: Marco Alvarez. Due: 2024-12-06.
- Temporary mitigation: lower RBAC migration concurrency during rolling upgrades and add preflight canary for event volume. Owner: Ethan Park (solutions), with product schedule. Due: 2024-12-04.

Medium-term work (3–8 weeks):
- Schema v2 release: publish audit schema spec, add migration guide for producers, linters, and test harness in CI. Owner: Priya Singh + Applied ML review. Due: 2025-01-15.
- SIEM exporter redesign: add priority retry queue and backpressure signal. Owner: Ava Martinez. Due: 2025-01-30.
- Chain-of-custody standard: draft internal spec for signed evidence tokens and storage retention classes (hot/cold/archival). Owner: Marco Alvarez + Security Compliance. Due: 2025-01-20.

Long-term (Q2+):
- Automate evidence completeness canaries: small synthetic RBAC change generator that writes a fixed correlation_id and verifies round-trip through ingest->normalize->export within SLA. Owner: Eng QA. Target: Q2 2025.
- Audit-log compression/archival policy with verifiable hashes per day to support legal forensics. Owner: Security Ops.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Legal retention vs. storage cost: what minimum retention for normalized vs raw evidence in high-sensitivity customers? (cc: finance, legal).
- KMS key management for signed evidence across private deployments (on-prem customers) — need migration plan.
- Does the SIEM partner accept additional retry semantics (rate-limited replays) or do we need to batch replays into a separate export endpoint?

Action tracker (short list):
- SEC-AT1: Update producer lib to enforce correlation_id. Owner: Liam Chen. Due: 2024-12-10.
- SEC-AT2: Add normalization-queue-depth alert. Owner: Zoe Carter. Due: 2024-12-01.
- SEC-AT3: Hotfix durable-staging for ingest offsets. Owner: Marco Alvarez. Due: 2024-12-06.
- SEC-AT4: Preflight canary for RBAC migration cadence. Owner: Ethan Park. Due: 2024-12-04.
- SEC-AT5: Draft chain-of-custody spec. Owner: Marco Alvarez. Due: 2025-01-20.

Notes to on-call and incident responders (quick reference):
- If you see normalization lag: do not cancel producer retries; instead increase normalizer candidates (k8s scale) and enable temporary ingest-throttling for non-forensic events via the router flag.
- Manual harvest steps: 1) snapshot audit bucket at time-range, 2) compute evidence_hash for each object, 3) sign snapshot token using ops-kms key, 4) upload to evidence cold storage path with metadata json (include actor_id/action/resource_id and any available correlation).
- Contact list for manual harvest: sec-oncall -> Marco, Zoe, Liam.

Postmortem writeup plan:
- This doc is the working retro; after short-term actions are completed, we will convert to a formal postmortem (final) and publish to Confluence. Include timeline, root cause analysis, impact, and follow-ups.

Appendix: suggested audit-schema example (single-line JSON example for producers):
{"timestamp":"2024-11-19T09:20:11Z","correlation_id":"c-8f7e2","actor_type":"service","actor_id":"rbac-migration-worker-3","action":"rbac.grant","resource_type":"workspace","resource_id":"ws-72","ip_address":"10.4.2.8","trace_id":"t-9a1b","rbac_delta":"+role:admin @user:alice","evidence_hash":"b62f..."}

If anything missing or you want to volunteer as owner for any item, please add a comment here or ping sec-oncall on Slack.

Document history:
- 2024-11-20 created by Priya Singh (initial notes)
- 2024-11-27 updated with timeline + immediate mitigations (Ethan, Marco)
- 2024-12-03 added action owners and deadlines (Zoe, Liam, Ava)
